newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger reaffirms plan to attend APEC.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger reaffirms plan to attend APEC.

text.p: Caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Wednesday reaffirmed he planned to attend the APEC leaders' forum in Manila in late November after winning conditional support to go from New Zealand First.
"That depends on where we are in terms of negotiation, but at the moment the planning is that I will go to APEC," Bolger said, going into the sixth round of coalition talks with New Zealand First.

New Zealand First holds the balance of power after an inconclusive election on October 12 and is negotiating with both the conservative National party and the main opposition Labour party over the shape of the next government.

In a statement issued after the fifth session of coalition talks on Tuesday nationalist New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said: "New Zealand First supports the attendance of whichever Prime Minister and ministers are holding office at the time of upcoming international meetings at which New Zealand is expected to be represented."
Peters said it was important to convey stability to the international community and there could only be one official government at any time.
The current coalition talks are expected to last until the end of November, making it likely Bolger will attend the APEC (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) forum on November 25.
New Zealand First has its sixth round of formal negotiations with the main opposition Labour party set down for Wednesday afternoon.
Meanwhile the National caucus on Tuesday endorsed Bolger as leader of the party. Bolger said he was "delighted, naturally" but the support of caucus was no surprise.
He said Deputy Prime Minister Don McKinnon initiated the vote of support.
McKinnon is touted as the frontrunner to replace Bolger as leader of National if the caucus opts for a change.
"It is required in our rules that we address the leadership issue shortly after each election and that's what we did," Bolger said. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
